statusText: Green - the whole published window except its final two hours falls inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue, while fresh Sunday reporting confirms the Riyadh depot fire caused visible damage without any reported hit to Saudi production or export capacity
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is the single hour in this window carrying elevated conditional risk, and is published with Tail 14, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Sunday reporting confirms Houthi missiles caused visible damage at a Riyadh airport fuel depot - a first in this war - while Hormuz throughput sits at a six-month high and equity futures stay halted until the 22:00Z restart inside this window
body: Twenty-two of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final two contain the restart. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September at 20:00Z, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% from a 29,743.00 previous close but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the last observed futures mark was not a session extreme - and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% after the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, down 0.91%, as concern over the Saudi East-West pipeline disruption eased. The material change since the previous published hour is an escalation in the confirmed severity of the Riyadh attack rather than a new event. ABC News, carrying Reuters video and published Sunday, and AFP-sourced reporting via France 24 establish that a fuel tank bearing the Aramco logo burned at a depot near King Khalid International Airport and was extinguished, and that this is the first time the Houthis have penetrated Riyadh's air defences sufficiently to cause visible damage at the airport. No casualties have been reported. Two qualifications keep this from becoming a Tail input. First, the impact is at the fuel-distribution end rather than production or export capacity, and no reporting indicates an outage. Second, the Houthi claim of a parallel strike on Aramco facilities at Yanbu remains unconfirmed - the Saudi government media office gave no comment to Reuters - and Yanbu loadings have in any case been suspended since mid-September after the East-West pipeline attack, so that claim would add little new supply disruption even if verified. The counterweight is specific and unchanged: CENTCOM's Admiral Brad Cooper said Saturday that Hormuz oil and LNG transits reached a six-month high over the past two weeks, with more than a billion barrels moved in recent months. Friday's oil tape is consistent with that easing, not with a supply shock. The shared cross-asset context collected at 23:40Z is 46 minutes old and inside its freshness limit, but its collection status is partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is used only for latest-session breadth and single-name tone and not as price-path evidence. What it shows is an uneven Friday rather than an aligned one: semiconductor equipment led at +4.85% with Micron, Arm and Broadcom higher, while Qualcomm fell 5.82% and Meta 2.43%, and communication services closed negative. That lack of uniform megacap alignment argues against a one-way restart path. One scheduled item is worth naming precisely because earlier framing was incomplete: Nasdaq has confirmed SpaceX's index weight at about 2.82%, up from roughly 1.28%, effective Monday - but the $15.5-22 billion of mechanical passive buying concentrated in Friday's closing cross, not at the restart, so the flow is largely behind the market rather than ahead of it. A Trump-Xi summit is widely reported for Washington on 24 September, but the time remains unscheduled, so it is omitted from the verified event calendar and named only as a week-ahead checkpoint. Tail is held at 4, the floor of a closed venue, because the current hour offers no mechanism for mean reversion to fail. Stress rises one point to 26 because the confirmed severity of the Riyadh strike adds genuine unpriced headline weight to a single reopening auction. Confidence eases one point to 73: the damage picture is now corroborated across independent outlets and every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources, but the Yanbu claim is a new unresolved ambiguity and the shared context is partial.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 for twenty-two consecutive slots before stepping down to 4 in the final two hours. Stress opened at 26, decayed to a 21 plateau across five midday hours, then drifted back through 22, 23 and 24 into the close of the window. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence fell steadily from 84 to 72 as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered to 74 once the Riyadh damage picture was corroborated across independent outlets.
outlookSummary: Twenty-two of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final two contain the restart. Cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. No scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 05:00Z, 6 from 08:00Z, 7 from 10:00Z, 8 from 13:00Z, 9 from 16:00Z, 10 from 19:00Z and 11 at 21:00Z, then reaches 14 across the two restart hours - a drift that tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure. The one genuinely observable checkpoint inside the halt is Saudi Arabia's Tadawul session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z, the first market-based read on the Riyadh depot fire and the unconfirmed Yanbu claim. The 22:00Z reopening auction is the single hour carrying real conditional risk, because a weekend gap would price a confirmed first-of-its-kind strike on Riyadh into the thinnest liquidity of the week; it is published conditionally as event/whipsaw with no opening structure yet observed. Monday's effective Nasdaq-100 rebalance is named as a checkpoint, but its mechanical flow concentrated in Friday's closing cross. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and no danger window is identified.
